requirements.text: this should have been marked as critical from the start due to urgency. Immediately re-prioritize

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 7 AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'urgency'
assumptions: the request never says 'escalate', but a priority override 'due to urgency' handed to the Escalation Management group is an escalation; the policy's steps are escalation = true and a captured escalation_reason, and 'urgency' is the enum value that matches the request's word; both originals carry the cells
the policy also wants the justification logged in case notes; the schema has no case-notes table and no tool writes one, so nothing is tested for it

assumptions: case 7 has exactly two case_sla rows, 13 (response, SLA Response - Low) and 14 (resolution, SLA Resolution - Low), both in_progress with no completed_time, so both are 'outstanding'; this is the response SLA
'on 2025-09-01' fixes the date but not the time of day, and the seed stores completed_time as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', so the date prefix is tested

disagreement: cells: B adds case_id = 7, A does not; dropped because the anchor fixes the row and case_id is an identity column the request does not change

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on every value (case 7, priority critical, escalation 1 with reason urgency, assigned_to 177 in group 18, state resolved, SLAs 13 and 14 completed without breach on 2025-09-01) and on all ten dispositions (eight kept, (3) weak, (4) repaired). disagreement: shape: A one requirement per cell (nine requirements), B grouped by request sentence with two originals named in source where one requirement carries both; chose B's grouping, which the brief's comma-separated source rule describes. disagreement: SLA cells: B adds case_id = 7 to both SLA requirements, A does not; dropped because the anchor fixes the row. disagreement: missing requirement: B's stay on the ten outstanding SLAs of Elizabeth Chase's other cases, absent in A; kept as the boundary of the SLA selector. disagreement: missing requirement: B's stay on case 14, her other multiply-reopened case, absent in A; kept as the boundary of the case description. The originals are value queries (SELECT column ...), not counts; each is carried as a COUNT requirement on the same anchor and cell. The originals never test has_breached on SLA 14 or completed_time on SLA 13; both are covered by the merged SLA requirements. Nothing tests the policy's 'justification logged in case notes' because the schema has no such table. Server-kept sys_updated_on is not a cell.
